prompt: A sharp, evenly-lit straight-on macro PHOTOGRAPH taken at eye level of a single tall clear glass GRADUATED MEASURING CYLINDER standing on a laboratory bench. The cylinder has a printed measuring scale up one side running from 0 mL at the bottom to 250 mL at the top, with numbered graduation lines every 50 mL (0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250) and small unnumbered tick marks in between. It is filled with brightly TINTED amber reagent whose flat liquid surface (the meniscus) rests at a level BETWEEN the 100 mL and 150 mL graduation lines, part-way between the two marks -- NOT resting on either labelled line. Draw the reagent surface as a clean, level horizontal line at that in-between height so a reader must interpolate its exact mL reading off the graduations. A genuine laboratory photograph: real glass with highlights, the coloured liquid and its flat surface clearly visible, clean bench lighting, soft shadow, no digital annotations, no printed numbers other than the scale graduations, no arrows or callouts.
